<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;">The new Customs Area Controller of the Apapa Area Command, Comptroller Murtala Muazu, has moved quickly to address operational friction at Nigeria’s busiest port, ordering a review of demand notice delays while putting training, stakeholder compliance and engagement with shipping lines on the command’s immediate agenda.<o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span>Muazu made the commitments on Monday, 5 October 2026, during his first stakeholder engagement at the command, where port users raised concerns about clearance delays, training gaps and operational challenges involving shipping companies.<o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">His early priorities point to a practical service delivery agenda: identify where the clearance chain is slowing down, strengthen the capacity of those operating within it and improve coordination among the actors responsible for moving cargo through Apapa.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><i><span lang="EN-US">“I want to make it clear to the trading public that I am here to strengthen the foundations that have already been laid,” Muazu said.</span></i><i><o:p></o:p></i></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><span lang="EN-US">TARGETING DEMAND NOTICE DELAYS</span></span><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Among the immediate issues identified was the processing of demand notices.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US"><img width="623" height="416" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," v:shapes="_x0000_i1025" style="margin-block: 16px;"></span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Stakeholders raised concerns about delays, prompting Muazu to direct a review of the process to determine where bottlenecks are occurring and what can be done to reduce them.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">“We will examine the process, identify any causes of delay and take steps to reduce or eliminate them, by the grace of God,” he said.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The directive places process efficiency at the centre of the new administration’s early agenda.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">For importers, exporters and licensed customs agents, predictable clearance procedures are critical. Delays in one part of the process can create further uncertainty across cargo movement and logistics planning.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The review therefore provides an opportunity for the command to look beyond individual complaints and determine whether procedural or operational gaps are contributing to avoidable delays.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><span lang="EN-US">TRAINING AS A SERVICE DELIVERY TOOL</span></span><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Muazu also identified knowledge and compliance gaps among participants in the clearance process as an area requiring attention.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Responding to stakeholder concerns about training, he said the command had developed a roadmap that would begin with releasing and examination officers before extending to importers, exporters and licensed customs agents.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The objective is to strengthen understanding of Customs procedures and compliance requirements across the clearance chain.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">That is significant because port efficiency depends not only on the performance of Customs officers but also on how effectively other participants understand and comply with the processes governing cargo clearance.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Where procedures, documentation or regulatory requirements are misunderstood, errors can create additional work and delays.&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Training can therefore serve as a service delivery intervention, strengthening both internal capacity and stakeholder understanding.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><span lang="EN-US">SHIPPING LINES ALSO ON THE AGENDA</span></span><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The CAC also responded to concerns about operational challenges involving shipping lines.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Muazu said the issues raised by stakeholders would form part of the command’s planned engagement with shipping companies, with the concerns to be formally presented as part of efforts to ease difficulties faced by port users.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The move recognises the interconnected nature of port operations.&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Customs is a critical part of the clearance process, but cargo movement also depends on the performance and coordination of other actors across the port ecosystem.&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Structured engagement with shipping lines could therefore help address operational issues that extend beyond Customs procedures and affect the wider experience of port users.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><span lang="EN-US">FROM STAKEHOLDER CONCERNS TO OPERATIONAL ACTION</span></span><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The significance of Muazu’s first engagement lies in the specificity of the issues identified.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Demand notice delays, training gaps and shipping line challenges are distinct problems, but they converge around one central question: how efficiently can cargo move through the Apapa system?</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The answer depends on the quality of processes, the capacity of the people operating them and the coordination between institutions and private sector participants.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Muazu’s stated approach is to address those points through targeted intervention while strengthening existing structures.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">For the Apapa Command, the next step will be translating those commitments into measurable improvements in the daily experience of port users.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">A review of demand notice processing will need to identify the source of delays and produce a more efficient process.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The training programme will need to improve understanding and reduce avoidable compliance errors.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Engagement with shipping lines will need to move beyond dialogue towards practical resolution of the concerns presented by stakeholders.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><img width="623" height="416" src="data:image/jpeg;base64," v:shapes="_x0000_i1026" style="margin-block: 16px;"><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><span lang="EN-US">THE TEST FOR THE NEW APAPA COMMAND</span></span><span style="font-weight: bolder;"><o:p></o:p></span></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Apapa occupies a critical position in Nigeria’s trade infrastructure, making the efficiency of its Customs operations relevant far beyond the command itself.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">For businesses moving cargo through the port, service delivery is ultimately measured through clearer procedures, predictable processing, effective communication and reduced delays.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">That makes implementation the real test of the new administration’s early agenda.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The stakeholder engagement has established the issues.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The review of demand notice processing provides an immediate operational test.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The training roadmap creates a pathway for strengthening capacity.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The planned engagement with shipping lines opens another channel for addressing challenges across the wider port ecosystem.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Together, these measures point towards a service delivery approach built around identifying friction points and addressing them directly.</span><o:p></o:p></p><h2 style="margin: 20px 0px 10px; font-weight: 600; font-family: &quot;Playfair Display&quot;, &quot;Playfair Display Fallback&quot;, Georgia, serif; --tw-font-weight: 600; color: rgb(21, 28, 46);"><span lang="EN-US">PrimeAxis Insight</span><o:p></o:p></h2><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Comptroller Muazu’s early agenda at Apapa Customs points to a simple but important reality: port efficiency is not created by one institution acting alone. It is created by how effectively the different parts of the clearance chain work together.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Demand notice processing, Customs examinations, documentation, compliance and shipping line operations may appear as separate processes. For the port user, however, they form one experience.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">A delay in one part can create friction across the chain.&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">That makes the review of demand notice processing more than an administrative exercise. If the command can identify the causes of delay and improve the process, it can remove one source of uncertainty from cargo clearance.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The proposed training programme carries similar significance. Better understanding of procedures among officers, importers, exporters and licensed customs agents can reduce avoidable errors and strengthen compliance before problems become delays.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Engagement with shipping lines is equally important because Customs cannot resolve every operational constraint within the port ecosystem on its own.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">The real measure of Muazu’s intervention, therefore, will not be the number of stakeholder meetings held or commitments announced. It will be whether port users experience clearer processes, better coordination and fewer avoidable delays.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">Apapa does not need efficiency in isolated parts. It needs efficiency across the chain.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">That is the test now facing the new Customs Area Controller.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">If the concerns raised by stakeholders can be converted into measurable improvements in clearance, compliance and coordination, Muazu’s early intervention will have moved beyond engagement into meaningful service delivery.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">For Nigeria’s most important port gateway, that is ultimately where the value lies.</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span><o:p></o:p></p><p class="MsoNormal" style="margin: 0px 0px 12px;"><span lang="EN-US">&nbsp;</span></p>
